target_customer: Wealth managers (RIAs, broker-dealers, multi-family offices) and fund managers that pay for software to offer and operate alternative investments
problem: Private equity and other alternatives run on manual paper and fax processes, which keeps smaller investors out and burdens advisors. Aqua provides software for subscriptions, reporting, documents and access vehicles.
business_model: B2B SaaS and platform fees to advisors and fund managers

founders.name: Rohan Marwaha
prior_employers: Blackstone (analyst, under a year per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: Education not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Dev Patel
founders.background_notes: Prior employer from the YC company page. CTO title from press summaries. Education not found.

competitors.name: iCapital Network
competitors.what: Platform giving wealth advisors and their clients access to alternative funds, with feeder fund operations
competitors.traction_then: not stated in the source opened

technical_complexity.rationale: Subscription document workflow, investor onboarding and fund operations software with custodian integrations; standard engineering with heavy compliance and integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration with advisors and fund sponsors and regulated fund structures raise switching costs, but iCapital and CAIS were far larger and well funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept growing; no source found that they copied or bought Aqua. Aqua remained independent and raised a Series A in September 2026.

market_need_then: In 2021 private equity access for individuals and advisors was a growth theme, with a TechCrunch piece (Nov 2021) citing manual processes. iCapital raised $440M in July 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses investwithaqua.com; the plain aqua name is crowded by unrelated companies.

identity.visual_style: An agency case study (Awesomic, undated) describes a brand and app redesign
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct B2B SaaS voice with coined category term TAIP (company site)

branding.brand_signature: Coined category label TAIP (Turnkey Alternative Investment Platform)

brand_strength.rationale: No consumer-facing brand coverage; generic name that shares search space with many other Aqua companies.

pivots.from: Marketplace giving individual investors access to private equity (2021)
pivots.to: B2B infrastructure for advisors and fund managers (TAIP)
pivots.why: Reframing visible in 2026 launch coverage; reasons not stated

outcome_analysis: Aqua is active. It raised a $2.5M seed in November 2021 led by Gradient Ventures, then no publicly reported round until a $15M Series A in September 2026 led by Arthur Ventures. It moved from an investor-facing private equity marketplace to infrastructure for advisors and fund managers and reports large transaction volume. It competes with far better funded iCapital and CAIS.
notes: Seed is $2.5M in TechCrunch (Nov 2021) but $3.8M in 2026 coverage (Wealth Management, Private Banker International); possibly later accounting of the same round or an extension, unexplained. Series A headline says $18.8M but body says $15M (total raised 18.8M). Other competitors (CAIS, Canoe, Moonfare, Yieldstreet) are named only in later or undated sources and are not listed. 2026 Series A is from sources dated Sept 2026.
